title: the lifecycle review's data-loss findings, fixed

findings.claim: LR-1: a restore whose rename aside fails (a mount point, EBUSY, or a signal between the two lines) had its put-back delete the live data folder, and on a folder that is not a mount point say "put back as it was" (OCR 1474-5); fixed: the put-back removes a folder only when its aside exists, and a mount-point target is refused before the first change

LR-11: the undo of a failed streamed image load removed every image and moved every tag another user of the engine had changed; fixed: the undo is scoped to the archive's tags and digests, what the load printed and what the bytes handed on name

LR-13: a hang-up with the terminal gone stopped the host step before the restore container was told, and the re-run swept the running restore's work folder; fixed: the signal is passed on first, the container has one name, and a second restore is refused while it exists

LR-15: with the engine's data root elsewhere the host restore passed no folder, restored the databases only and reported success; fixed: each volume's folder is asked of the engine and a missing one is refused before anything stops

LR-16: a box whose lake is in restic could not be restored or verified by the documented commands (options not named, verify saw the file alone, restore locked a read-only repository); fixed: both runbook pages name the options, verify mounts the folder, the restore passes --no-lock

LR-2: deploy/poc.sh, in every box's host tree, ran compose down -v on the installed site's project at reset (and acted on it at every other action); fixed: every action is refused before anything runs when deploy/updates/installed.json exists

LR-10: rollback after a kill in refdata or finish restored the pre-update databases over a checked release in service, losing every row written since; fixed: those two steps are finished forward with the full health check, and a failure stops in a named state without a rollback
LR-16 (c): the restore with --no-lock against a real restic binary on a read-only bind is not run here (no restic in this container); shown only against a stand-in that models the lock rule
